case_name: State Of Himachal Pradesh v Manoj Kumar @ Chhotu
respondent:
Manoj Kumar @ Chhotu
Supreme Court of India

29 September 2008
Criminal Appeal No. 1549 Of 2008 (Arising Out Of S.L.P. (Crl.) No.1546 Of 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : HON'BLE JUSTICE DR. ARIJIT PASAYAT
1. Leave granted.
2. Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Himachal Pradesh High Court dismissing the application filed in terms of S. 378(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The respondent faced trial for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 376/511 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. The Trial Court found that the accusations were not established and directed his acquittal giving him the benefit of doubt. An application for grant of leave in terms of S. 378 of the Code was filed which was dismissed summarily stating "Dismissed".
3. According to learned counsel for the appellant-State it was imperative on the High Court to indicate reasons as to why the prayer for grant of leave was found
facts: The respondent faced trial for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 376/511 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The Trial Court found that the accusations were not established and directed his acquittal giving him the benefit of doubt.
The application for grant of leave in terms of S. 378 of the Code was filed which was dismissed summarily stating 'Dismissed'.
The trial Court on the facts of the case did not perform its duties, as was enjoined on it by law.
issues: Whether the High Court was correct in dismissing the application for grant of leave without giving any reasons?
petitioner_arguments: It was imperative on the High Court to indicate reasons as to why the prayer for grant of leave was found untenable.
In the absence of any such reasons, the order of the High Court is indefensible.
The requirement of indicating reasons in such cases has been judicially recognised as imperative.
court_reasoning: The giving of reasons is one of the fundamentals of good administration
Reasons are live links between the mind of the decision taker to the controversy in question and the decision or conclusion arrived at
Right to reason is an indispensable part of a sound judicial system, reasons at least sufficient to indicate an application of mind to the matter before Court.
holding: The impugned judgment of the High Court is unsustainable and is set aside.
We grant leave to the State to file the appeal.

The High Court shall entertain the appeal and after formal notice to the respondent hear the appeal and dispose it of in accordance with law, uninfluenced by any observation made in the present appeal.
